title: The Only App That Helps Me Organize My Whole Life
body:
Amazing Marvin is the only app I’ve found that truly helps me manage my life. Once you take the time to explore its settings, you can shape it around the way you think and work. There are so many options that you can build a system for virtually every area of your life.

I’ve had a lifetime subscription and have been using Marvin for about four years. I’ve tried Notion and many other planning apps, but none of them compare for me. I only wish more people knew about it!

title: Great on desktop and mobile
body: Great app for people who want customizable task and project management software. Lots of options available for those with neurodivergence.
author: Arianimal

title: Charged me $240 for training and then didn’t show up
body: The company that runs this is horrible.  For people with ADHD, the app is very elaborate.  I was willing to pay for special training so I could figure out how to use it, and when I inquired, I was connected to the founder of the app, who has a website where you pay $240 for an hour of her time.  I paid it and then her calendar was broken so I couldn’t book a time. When I inquired by email, someone said they would let her know and then it was radio silence from there.
author: Bhk416

title: Complimentary tool with desktop program.
body: I’ve read the mediocre reviews on here and feel I should share my experience. The app is only a barebones version of the PC. The program and app seem to be in regular updates, so if it isn’t working for you now, it might at a later date. I still think the app is an excellent part of the entire AM tool kit. I would recommend this in conjunction with the PC version. AM has changed my academic and regular life significantly for the better. There is well set up systems that are a great place to start but AM really shows off in the customization of the system. It took months of trying different combinations of strategies. The developer is very good about answering questions quickly. I’ve tried several of the other task management/productivity apps and all of them pale in comparison to the features and functions that Amazing Marvin has overall. AM has time tracking for each task, time blocking, duration estimates, scheduling, planning, soft deadlines, task dependencies, to do lists, agendas, methods for helping prioritize tasks, and the list goes on. Being able to set time blocks and have the tasks I have scheduled for the day automatically set into their category connected to the time block has been a game changer. I highly recommend this program and by extension, the app, for anyone struggling with time management. It has not occurred to me that there would be an expectation for the full features in the mobile app. The app has been working extremely well in the capacity that I have been using it for (as a supplementary tool), so I hope this review helps in understanding the program and app as it is at the time of this review.

title: Deep Learning
body: I’m still using a trial version but for sure can tell the app will finally get me where I have been wanting to go for improving my productivity. Web version is good but mobile version sucks. It does dot adopt the screen orientation and fixed at portrait view only.
author: DataSync

title: Complicated, cumbersome; suitable for power users
body:
Un-intuitive at the start. It requires too much customisation, and even then, some crucial functionality like creation of recurring tasks can not be done on the mobile.

It is simply not possible to make quick entries or quickly edit existing ones.

A fundamental need of sorting is also complicated: auto-sorting is strange, restrictive or requires frequent manual sorting.
